evidence.statement: NVIDIA announced the Vera Rubin platform as six new chips designed together as one AI supercomputer: Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU and Spectrum-6 Ethernet switch.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA Kicks Off the Next Generation of AI With Rubin

evidence.statement: NVIDIA announced seven Rubin platform chips in full production and described the platform as including Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU, Spectrum-6 Ethernet and Groq 3 LPX.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Opens Agentic AI Frontier

evidence.statement: NVIDIA’s Rubin architecture description specifies HBM4, up to 288 GB per GPU, 12-Hi stacks, up to 22 TB/s of memory bandwidth, NVLink 6 at 3,600 GB/s and liquid-cooled NVL72 infrastructure.
NVIDIA describes NVL72 as integrating 72 Rubin GPUs, 36 Vera CPUs, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs and NVLink 6 in a rack-scale platform.
NVIDIA’s Blackwell materials describe Blackwell’s higher-bandwidth HBM3E memory and fifth-generation NVLink technology, providing the documented baseline for the Rubin comparison.
Micron announced HBM4 36GB 12H in high-volume production, designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, and said it had begun volume shipment in the first quarter of 2026.
evidence.source_title: Micron HBM4 for NVIDIA Vera Rubin

evidence.statement: SK hynix and NVIDIA announced a multi-year technology partnership that includes developing memory for NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI supercomputers.
evidence.source_title: SK hynix and NVIDIA Multi-year Technology Partnership

evidence.statement: Samsung announced HBM4 mass production and commercial shipments; this establishes HBM4 capability but does not by itself establish a Rubin design win.

NVIDIA describes Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics co-packaged optical switch systems as part of the Rubin networking path, with stated power-efficiency and uptime improvements compared with traditional methods.
NVIDIA describes Rubin systems as liquid-cooled and identifies the data center as the unit of compute; this establishes a platform design dependency, not a measured cooling or power shortage.
The IEA reports that AI-focused data centers are geographically concentrated and that grid connection queues and power-system constraints can delay planned data-center projects.

TSMC describes CoWoS as integrating SoC chips and HBM stacks and identifies advanced packaging as a production capability; this supports a general package dependency but does not establish TSMC as a Rubin supplier.

NVIDIA says Rubin is being manufactured and shipped with Taiwan server makers and global supply-chain leaders, and describes an ecosystem of more than 80 MGX partners; it does not name every Rubin relationship.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Platform Supply Chain Description

evidence.statement: NVIDIA names TSMC, SPIL, Kinsus, KYEC and UMTC as key wafer and chip partners in the Vera Rubin supply chain, and names Foxconn, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology, Wistron and Inventec among manufacturing and systems leaders; the source does not assign each company a specific Rubin component or output volume.
evidence.source_title: Taiwan’s Industry Titans Turbocharge World’s AI Infrastructure Buildout With NVIDIA

evidence.statement: Foxconn says it exhibited full-system AI server racks for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and later announced production in Europe of advanced AI systems with the Rubin platform; it does not disclose Rubin shipment volume.
evidence.source_title: Foxconn and Bull Advance European AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72

evidence.statement: NVIDIA quotes Lenovo saying it is embracing the next-generation Rubin platform and leveraging its Neptune liquid-cooling solution, manufacturing efficiency and service reach; this does not establish a Rubin shipment schedule or allocation.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA Kicks Off the Next Generation of AI With Rubin

evidence.statement: Vertiv announced its role in advancing power and cooling designs for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI-factory reference design, including simulation-ready infrastructure models and validated interfaces; this is a design relationship, not proof of deployment at every Rubin site.
evidence.source_title: Vertiv Brings Converged Physical Infrastructure to NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factories

evidence.statement: NVIDIA says Vera Rubin NVL72 production is ramping with racks running at partners CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius; this identifies operators hosting or running systems, not suppliers or builders.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Driving Performance per Watt for Partners Worldwide
